subject: math
explanation: Decimals can be written using negative exponents of 10. Moving the decimal point one place left multiplies by 10⁻¹. Since 12² = 144, we can find powers of decimal numbers by adjusting place value: (1.2)² = (12/10)² = 144/100 = 1.44; (0.12)² = 144/10000 = 0.0144; (0.012)² = 0.000144; and 120² = 144 × 100 = 14400. The exponent on 10 tracks how many places the decimal shifted. This links ordinary decimals to the laws of exponents.

brainstorming.question: If 12² = 144, why is (0.12)² much smaller than 1.44?
brainstorming.answer: 0.12 = 12/100, so squaring gives 144/10000 — dividing by 100 twice makes the result 100 times smaller than (1.2)².

brainstorming.question: How does 10⁻¹ relate to the decimal 0.1?
brainstorming.answer: 10⁻¹ = 1/10 = 0.1 — each negative step on the power of 10 moves the decimal point left.

brainstorming.question: Can every decimal be written with powers of 10?
brainstorming.answer: Many can, especially those with finitely many digits after the decimal point, by expressing each place as a power of 10.

misconceptions.correct: (0.12)² = 0.0144 — squaring 0.12 means 0.12 × 0.12, not just moving the decimal one place.
10⁻² = 1/100 = 0.01 — negative exponent means reciprocal, not a negative number.
Rewrite decimals as fractions with powers of 10, then apply the same laws.

realLifeConnections.title: Currency and cents
realLifeConnections.description: ₹1.20 = 1.2 × 10⁰ rupees; small price differences use decimal powers implicitly.

realLifeConnections.title: Scientific measurements
realLifeConnections.description: A cell width of 0.00001 m is written as 1×10⁻⁵ m — decimals become clean powers of 10.

realLifeConnections.title: Engineering tolerances
realLifeConnections.description: Machine parts specified to 0.001 cm precision use negative powers of 10 for accuracy.

realLifeConnections.title: Digital displays
realLifeConnections.description: Multiplying a decimal reading by 10² shifts two places right — like converting metres to centimetres.

realLifeConnections.title: Medicine dosages
realLifeConnections.description: A dose of 0.25 mg can be expressed as 2.5×10⁻¹ mg for scientific calculation.

activities.title: Decimal square table
activities.instructions: Given 12² = 144, complete a table for (1.2)², (0.12)², (0.012)², and 120² by tracking powers of 10.

activities.title: Place-value expansion
activities.instructions: Expand 5642 and 0.0056 as sums of terms like a×10ⁿ. Identify each digit's place using exponents.

activities.title: Calculator check
activities.instructions: Compute (0.12)² on a calculator and verify it matches 144/10000 from exponent reasoning.

quiz.question: 172 = 1×10² + 7×10¹ + 2×10⁰ shows:
quiz.explanation: Each digit is multiplied by a power of 10 matching its place.

quiz.question: Moving decimal 2 places left divides by:
quiz.explanation: Each place left divides by 10; two places divides by 10².
